item.text: {"text":"Meta’s 2024 HSTU reference configuration uses sampled softmax with 128 negatives, temperature 0.05, and L2-normalized item/user representations—useful objective choices to test while retaining the HSTU backbone. These MovieLens settings are a starting point, not evidence of optimality on the four Amazon categories. [Official configuration](https://github.com/meta-recsys/generative-recommenders/blob/main/configs/ml-1m/hstu-sampled-softmax-n128-final.gin). RecSys 2025’s *Correcting the LogQ Correction* shows that in-batch sampling disproportionately penalizes popular items; its refined correction accounts for the positive being always present rather than sampled. Sampling correction must match the actual proposal distribution; applying ordinary logQ correction blindly to mined negatives is unjustified. [Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.09331).\n\nPractical hypothesis: compare uniform multi-negative sampled softmax against a mixture of uniform and moderately hard negatives scored by the same HSTU, gradually increasing hardness and excluding observed training positives. Treat this as an experiment: false negatives can represent real interests, so selecting only the highest-scoring unseen items risks suppressing relevant recommendations. [False-negative research](https://arxiv.org/abs/2208.04116). More negatives also compete with batch size: a 2026 preprint reports advantages from larger batches under its fixed batch-times-negatives memory budget, rather than universally maximizing negative count. [Preprint](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.11061). The supplied Electronics statistic—10.71% of negatives outranking positives—motivates investigation but does not establish its cause. Select experiments using the unchanged macro validation HR@10, with one trained HSTU checkpoint per category; larger training margins alone do not establish ranking generalization."}
